verdict_basis: Round 16 (cron) resolved R15's one deferral - the golden-age full-2D source hunt - by leaving the YouTube lane entirely: archive.org is yt-dlp-compatible via the existing run_on_dell.sh meta/fetch path, free, and held complete restored prints where YouTube only surfaces abridged WB Kids cuts (215-294s vs the 395-415s films). Two full films fetched+measured on the Dell, both label-integrity PASS via the free muse vision lane: anim-whats-opera-doc ('What's Opera, Doc? - (1957, Restored)', archive.org id whats-opera-doc-1957-restored, uploader weegeelook4, upload 2024-06-01, 410.743s, 794x576 @23.976; 96 cuts / 40 hard, first cut 35.87s, 0.2362 cps, median shot 3.003s, mean 4.234s, p5 0.818 / p95 11.061, min 0.25 / max 35.868; motion 0.1048, stillness 0.141; luma 0.406, sat 0.543 = class-A high (beats Powers of Ten 0.530), n80 5; -23.1 LUFS, LRA 10.8, TP -5.9; description_head '*Restored HBO Max (Max) US print') and anim-duck-amuck ('Duck Amuck - (1953, Restored)', archive.org id duck-amuck-1953-restored, same uploader, upload 2024-05-26, 415.039s, 768x576 @23.976; 46 cuts / 19 hard, first cut 147.397s, 0.1132 cps, shot mean 8.831s but median 0.084s = corpus minimum by 3.5x, p5 0.083 / p95 46.547, min 0.083 / max 147.397; motion 0.077, stillness 0.138; luma 0.64 white-paper world (#eff1ec palette tile 29.1%), sat 0.383, n80 5; -23.1 LUFS = exactly the corpus median, LRA 11.3, TP -5.6). FINDINGS (measured-rule revision, R3/R6/R11/R13/R14/R15 precedent): (1) golden-age Technicolor cel cuts like live action - Opera Doc's 96 detector events match real scene changes on-sheet, so R15's 'cel animation reads silent' is SCOPED to 1928 rubber-hose cel (Steamboat); the class-A invalidity ladder gains an ERA axis: paper redraw floods (any era) < 1928 rubber-hose cel silent < golden-age cel VALID (1950s) = replacement stop-motion VALID - two invalid rungs, two valid rungs, each identified by technique+era. (2) Duck Amuck is the corpus's first BURST grammar - a ~26-shot run of literal 2-frame (0.083s) shots (the animator's strobe/erase gags - cuts AS content) drops median shot to 0.084s while takes run 147.4s/107.7s/49.7s between bursts; mean 8.8s vs median 0.084s is the burst signature; the detector reads the film's real meta-structure, but median shot is meaningless for burst films - read the lens distribution (p5/p95). TOOLING DEFECT FOUND+FIXED IN-ROUND: the receipt-completeness gate was YouTube-shaped (required source.channel; archive.org extracts key attribution as uploader with channel null) - verify_receipts.py widened to accept channel-or-uploader; both new receipts initially FAILed, all 74 PASS after the fix. Envelope re-ranged at n=9 programmatically: duration 100.9-647.8 med 410.7; cps 0.0065-0.793 med 0.113; median shot 0.084-131.4 med 3.003; motion 0.031-0.157 med 0.080; stillness 0.064-0.419 med 0.138; luma 0.080-0.861 med 0.406; sat 0.0-0.543 med 0.383; LUFS -26.3..-10.8 med -23.1 (modern normalized restorations); LRA 3.5-24.7 med 10.8; n80 4-5 med 4. Corpus now 74 receipts = 69 reference films + 5 own. Superseded R15 claims preserved on record (era-scoping addendum + round log added, nothing deleted). Disposition: the round's own gate defect was found, fixed, and re-verified green in-round (72 -> 74 receipts all-pass post-fix), so ship with the defect+fix documented per the measured-revision precedent and a dedicated tooling-defect gate.

2/2 new sheets read at judge time via free muse vision lane (opencode muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free, run from .media/sheets): Opera Doc sheet (41-tile montage) -> golden-age Technicolor cel: Bugs Bunny as Brunhilde with winged helmet and spear, Elmer as Siegfried in horned helmet, licensed WB character designs, saturated painted backgrounds, 41/41 tiles genuine; Duck Amuck sheet (41-tile montage) -> Daffy Duck meta-cartoon: Daffy arguing with the animator's off-screen pencil/eraser, background style gags (farm scene, anime-style, white void), frame-line/strobe frames visible, 1940s-50s WB cel look, ~41/41 genuine.

Both muse reads matched the requested class (golden-age Technicolor cel, 1950s WB) BEFORE measurement was trusted, and both matched the named films specifically (Opera Doc's Wagnerian staging; Duck Amuck's animator-vs-duck premise). Source vetting on record: a 411s YouTube 'Duck Amuck (1953) Fan dub' was DISQUALIFIED on label integrity (replaced soundtrack would corrupt loudness receipts); EVd-mxb53A8 'Bugs Bunny at the Hollywood Bowl' deprioritized (possible 1979 special material); archive.org restored HBO Max prints chosen instead (description_head '*Restored HBO Max (Max) US print' recorded in both receipts; restoration caveat: -23.1 LUFS both films is modern normalization, not 1950s master levels).

REAL rig defect found this round: rig/verify_receipts.py receipt-completeness gate was YouTube-shaped - it required source.channel, but archive.org yt-dlp extracts populate uploader (channel null), so both new receipts FAILed completeness on first verify. Fixed in-round: gate now accepts channel OR uploader ('fetched clip missing title/channel-or-uploader/webpage_url'), with a comment noting the attribution mapping. Re-run: 74/74 PASS. No other rig changes ('anim-' prefix already maps to class A in summarize.py); archive.org details URLs needed no rig changes at all (meta/fetch are yt-dlp-compatible).

No full video watched (41-tile contact sheets only); both prints are 2000s-era HBO Max restorations at 576p (era artifacts smoothed; loudness/luma are restoration masters, caveated in PLAYBOOK and receipts); Duck Amuck's median-shot minimum is a burst-grammar artifact, not an edit-rate claim (rule 1 revised to say median is meaningless for burst films); Duck Amuck sheet read reported ~41/41 (one tile ambiguity at montage density); archive.org advancedsearch discovery needed a query rephrase (first attempt returned empty); no keys, no paid lanes, Dell-only media, round inside the ~30min budget.
